ai.description: This slender, 15–20 cm worm snake is uniform dark brown to black with a pale snout. It is distinguished by 20 midbody scale rows and a rounded, blunt tail lacking a terminal spine.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Indotyphlops meszoelyi* is best distinguished by its unique head scalation, specifically the presence of a single preocular scale that is in contact with the second supralabial.
ai.habitat: The Darjeeling Worm Snake inhabits moist, high-altitude temperate forests and tea plantations in the Eastern Himalayas, typically found at elevations between 1,500–2,200m.
ai.behavior: The Darjeeling worm snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending most of its time burrowing through soil and leaf litter in search of ant and termite larvae.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Indotyphlops meszoelyi* is oviparous, laying small clutches of eggs. While specific breeding details are limited, it likely reproduces during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Indotyphlops meszoelyi* is endemic to the Darjeeling district of West Bengal, India, where it is found at elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
